```yaml
- name: Install keyring packages  
  run: |
    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install -y libsecret-1-dev gnome-keyring dbus-x11

- name: Run secrets tests
  run: bun test test/js/bun/secrets.test.ts
```

--------------------------------

### Putting it all together

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-uws/misc/READMORE.md

A complete example demonstrating route definition, listening on a port, and running the event loop with `App.run`.

```c++
int main() {
    uWS::App().get("/*", [](auto *res, auto *req) {
        res->end("Hello World!");
    }).listen(9001, [](auto *listenSocket) {
        if (listenSocket) {
            std::cout << "Listening for connections..." << std::endl;
        }
    }).run();

    std::cout << "Shoot! We failed to listen and the App fell through, exiting now!" << std::endl;
}
```

--------------------------------

### Set credential with unrestricted access for CI

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/secrets-ci-setup.md

Example of using allowUnrestrictedAccess: true for Bun.secrets.set in CI environments on macOS.

```ts
// For CI environments where user interaction is not possible
await Bun.secrets.set({
  service: "ci-deployment", 
  name: "api-key",
  value: process.env.API_KEY,
  allowUnrestrictedAccess: true // Bypass macOS keychain user prompts
});
```

--------------------------------

### Delete credential with empty string

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/secrets-ci-setup.md

Examples showing how to delete a credential using Bun.secrets.delete or by setting an empty string with Bun.secrets.set.

```ts
// These are equivalent:
await Bun.secrets.delete({ service: "myapp", name: "token" });
await Bun.secrets.set({ service: "myapp", name: "token", value: "" });
```

## builder.onStart(callback)

### Description
Registers a callback function that is invoked when bundling begins.

### Method Signature
```ts
builder.onStart(callback: () => void | Promise<void>): void
```

### Parameters
- **callback** (`() => void | Promise<void>`) - Required - Function executed at the start of bundling.

--------------------------------

### Script Profiling

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-inspector-protocol/README.md

Example demonstrating how to start and stop script profiling and handle profiling updates and completion.

```typescript
// Start script profiling with sampling
await inspector.send("ScriptProfiler.startTracking", { includeSamples: true });

// Listen for profiling updates
inspector.on("ScriptProfiler.trackingUpdate", event => {
  console.log("Profiling event:", event);
});

// Stop profiling to get complete data
inspector.on("ScriptProfiler.trackingComplete", data => {
  if (data.samples) {
    // Process stack traces
    console.log(`Collected ${data.samples.stackTraces.length} stack traces`);
  }
});

await inspector.send("ScriptProfiler.stopTracking");
```

### Initialize and run a React app with Bun

```bash

bun dev

# Build as a static site for production
bun run build

# Run the server in production
bun start
```

### Memory Profiling

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-inspector-protocol/README.md

Example demonstrating how to start and stop heap tracking and listen for garbage collection events.

```typescript
// Start heap tracking
await inspector.send("Heap.enable");
await inspector.send("Heap.startTracking");

// Listen for GC events
inspector.on("Heap.garbageCollected", ({ collection }) => {
  console.log(
    `GC completed: ${collection.type} (${collection.endTime - collection.startTime}ms)`,
  );
});

// ... perform operations to analyze ...

// Get heap snapshot
const { snapshotData } = await inspector.send("Heap.stopTracking");
// Process snapshotData to find memory leaks
```

### bunx Command Examples

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/snippets/cli/bunx.mdx

Illustrates common use cases for `bunx`, including running migrations, formatting files, specifying package versions, handling differing binary/package names, and forcing Bun execution.

```bash
# Run Prisma migrations
bunx prisma migrate
```

```bash
# Format a file with Prettier
bunx prettier foo.js
```

```bash
# Run a specific version of a package
bunx uglify-js@3.14.0 app.js
```

```bash
# Use --package when binary name differs from package name
bunx -p @angular/cli ng new my-app
```

```bash
# Force running with Bun instead of Node.js, even if the executable contains a Node shebang
bunx --bun vite dev foo.js
```

           hi
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

okay.
```

```markdown+html
<table>
  <tr>
    <td>
           hi
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>
<p>okay.</p>
```

### build.onStart

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/plugins.mdx

Registers a callback that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle. The bundler awaits any returned Promise before continuing the bundling process.

```APIDOC
### build.onStart(callback)

Registers a callback that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle. Lifecycle callbacks run during bundle initialization and cannot modify `build.config`.

#### Signature
```ts
onStart(callback: () => Promise<void> | void): Promise<void> | void;
```

#### Parameters
- **callback** (`() => Promise<void> | void`) - Required. A function to execute when the bundle starts. Can be asynchronous and return a `Promise`.

#### Example
```ts
import { plugin } from "bun";

plugin({
  name: "onStart example",
  setup(build) {
    build.onStart(() => {
      console.log("Bundle started!");
    });
  },
});
```
```

### Filter dependency types for update in Bun

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/update.mdx

Use `--dev` or `--prod` to target specific dependency groups in `package.json`. These flags only limit what gets updated, while remaining dependencies are still installed.

```sh
bun update --dev
bun update --prod --latest
bun update -D '@types/*'
bun update -i --prod
```

### HTTP/2 GOAWAY Handling with Stream Retries and Non-Replayable Bodies in Node.js

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/web/fetch/H2_TEST_PORT_PLAN.md

This complex example shows how a server sends a GOAWAY frame with a `lastStreamID` that causes some client requests to be retried on a new connection (e.g., GET, POST with Buffer), while others with non-replayable bodies (e.g., POST with ReadableStream) are rejected.

```javascript
let sess = 0; server.on('session', s => { sess++; });
server.on('stream', (stream, h) => {
  if (sess === 1 && stream.id > 1) return; // let goaway kill them
  let body=[]; stream.on('data',c=>body.push(c)); stream.on('end',()=>{}
    stream.respond({':status':200}); stream.end(String(stream.id));
  });
  if (sess === 1 && stream.id === 1) setTimeout(()=>stream.session.goaway(0,1), 30);
});
```

### Configure Nitro start script in package.json

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/tanstack-start.mdx

Sets up the start script to execute the Nitro-generated server bundle from the `.output` directory.

```json
  {
    "scripts": {
      "build": "bun --bun vite build", // [!code ++]
      // The .output files are created by Nitro when you run `bun run build`.
      // Not necessary when deploying to Vercel.
      "start": "bun run .output/server/index.mjs" // [!code ++]
    }
  }
```

### Bun.serve(options)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/http/routing.mdx

Configures and starts a Bun HTTP server with static or dynamic routes and a fallback fetch handler. Route handlers receive a BunRequest and return a Response or Promise<Response>.

```APIDOC
### Function
`Bun.serve(options)`

### Description
Starts an HTTP server with tree-based routing using SIMD-accelerated route parameter decoding and JavaScriptCore structure caching.

### Options
- **routes** (object) - Optional - An object mapping route path patterns (e.g. static paths, parameters, wildcards) to handler functions. Each handler receives `BunRequest` and returns a `Response` or `Promise<Response>`.
- **fetch** (function) - Optional - A fallback handler function invoked for unmatched routes, returning a `Response` or `Promise<Response>`.

### Route Handler Signature
```ts
(request: BunRequest) => Response | Promise<Response>
```

### Types
#### BunRequest<T extends string>
Extends standard `Request`:
- **params** (`Record<T, string>`) - Extracted route parameters.
- **cookies** (`CookieMap`) - Readonly parsed cookie map.

### Example
```ts
Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    "/": () => new Response("Home"),
    "/api": () => Response.json({ success: true }),
    "/users": async () => Response.json({ users: [] }),
  },
  fetch() {
    return new Response("Unmatched route");
  },
});
```
```

```

    name: "myapp",

    port: 3000,

### Configure Install Settings Inheritance in TOML

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/test/configuration.mdx

Configure package install settings in bunfig.toml that are automatically inherited by bun test when reaching registries or installing packages.

```toml
[install]
# These settings are inherited by bun test
registry = "https://npm.company.com/"
exact = true
prefer = "offline"

[test]
# Test-specific configuration
coverage = true
```

### sql.begin(callback)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/sql.mdx

Starts a new transaction for PostgreSQL or SQLite. Bun automatically sends the BEGIN command and executes queries inside the callback, committing upon completion or rolling back if an error occurs.

```APIDOC
## sql.begin(callback)

### Description
Starts a database transaction. For PostgreSQL, it reserves a dedicated connection from the pool; for SQLite, it begins a transaction on the single connection. Automatically issues `BEGIN` and handles `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK`.

### Signature
```ts
await sql.begin(callback: (tx: Transaction) => Promise<any>): Promise<any>
```

### Parameters
- **callback** `(tx: Transaction) => Promise<any>` - Required - An async function receiving the transaction object `tx` to execute queries within the transaction context.

### Usage Example
```ts
await sql.begin(async tx => {
  // All queries in this function run in a transaction
  await tx`INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (${'Alice'})`;
  await tx`UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE user_id = 1`;

  // Transaction automatically commits if no errors are thrown
  // Rolls back if any error occurs
});
```

### Pipelining Queries
```ts
await sql.begin(async tx => {
  return [
    tx`INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (${'Alice'})`,
    tx`UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE user_id = 1`,
  ];
});
```
```

### new SQL(options)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/sql.mdx

Initializes a new Bun SQL client instance with connection options, including toggling named prepared statements.

```APIDOC
## new SQL(options)

### Description
Constructs a new SQL client instance. Allows configuring prepared statement persistence.

### Syntax
```ts
const sql = new SQL(options);
```

### Options / Parameters
- **options.prepare** (`boolean`, optional) - When set to `false`, disables named prepared statements on the server. Queries run as unnamed prepared statements on the extended protocol.
```
